nodes.label: CyberAlchemy
nodes.plain_language: The Product that must make bounded composite work possible.
nodes.claim: A source-bound Product projection anchors this capability without redefining CyberAlchemy.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the capability, an orchestrator, an implementation, or product proof.

nodes.label: Execute Bounded Composite Work
nodes.plain_language: Let people and systems combine bounded work into one reusable, observable, replayable work boundary.
nodes.claim: CyberAlchemy needs stable product meaning for bounded work composition before selecting an orchestration realization.

source_refs.selector: A Product Capability is a stable, owner-qualified statement
Any finite or explicitly bounded workflow

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus work-orchestration capability owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not RWO, a workflow definition, scheduler, journal, command, permission, runtime process, or adoption decision.
open_questions: Which first bounded workflow will test product value after the construction chain becomes eligible?

nodes.label: Work Author
nodes.plain_language: A participant who describes typed work, composition, inputs, outputs, limits, and owner boundaries.
nodes.claim: Authorship defines candidate structure but does not grant execution or effect authority.
nodes.owner_route: Owner of each bounded workflow definition
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not automatically the work operator, domain decision owner, runtime owner, or effect authorizer.

nodes.label: Work Operator
nodes.plain_language: A participant responsible for invoking and observing one accepted bounded-work realization.
nodes.claim: Operation occurs only under a later exact implementation and authority binding.
nodes.owner_route: Future accepted work-orchestration runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a product owner, work author, universal administrator, or authority source.
open_questions: Which runtime owner will accept the first realization boundary?

nodes.label: Work Consumer
nodes.plain_language: A participant that consumes a composite output or structural execution record for one stated use.
nodes.claim: A consumer receives bounded output without acquiring authority over its sources or producers.
nodes.owner_route: Owner of each bounded use
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Consumption is not ownership, acceptance, publication, or permission to execute another effect.

nodes.label: Bounded Composition
nodes.plain_language: Finite or explicitly limited work can be composed and reused through one typed outer boundary.
nodes.claim: Recursive composition remains structurally closed without recursive authority.
nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 work-orchestration capability owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not proof that arbitrary recursion terminates or that nested composites may launch schedulers.

nodes.label: Replayable Structural Routing
nodes.plain_language: Structural progress can be reconstructed from exact accepted history and a versioned reducer.
nodes.claim: Replay concerns routing state only and preserves historical inputs and versions.

source_refs.selector: rebuild its routing cursor from the accepted event history

nodes.owner_route: Future accepted-history owner plus work-orchestration runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not current revalidation, redelivery authority, leaf-domain truth, or effect success.
open_questions: Which exact source owns accepted work history?

nodes.label: Authority-Preserving Execution
nodes.plain_language: Composition and routing preserve each work unit's domain, communication, evidence, and effect boundaries.
nodes.claim: Parentage and graph connectivity cannot transfer authority.

source_refs.selector: Parentage does not transmit tools, context, budget, evidence, or authority

nodes.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus applicable domain and authority owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an authority grant, permission registry, or proof that an adapter is authorized.

nodes.label: Work Definition Input Contract
nodes.plain_language: The required immutable work identity, schemas, topology, limits, mappings, event contracts, and authority references for one invocation.
nodes.claim: Missing, stale, ambiguous, or unknown required input blocks materialization.
nodes.owner_route: Future DomainSpec work-orchestration profile owner plus work-definition owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a command, run, attempt, implementation binding, or authority decision.

nodes.label: Structural Execution Record Contract
nodes.plain_language: A bounded output containing exact run identity, accepted-history reference, cursor version, structural terminal posture, and artifact references.
nodes.claim: The record reports structural evidence without upgrading domain or effect claims.
nodes.owner_route: Future work-orchestration evidence owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not business completion, approval, artifact admission, implementation conformance, or external-effect success.

nodes.label: Single Root Authority Policy
nodes.plain_language: One root runtime expands and schedules one graph; nested composites never launch an independently authoritative scheduler.
nodes.claim: Recursive composition must not become recursive execution authority.
nodes.owner_route: Work-orchestration runtime owner plus execution-authority owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a claim that the root owns domain decisions or external effects.

nodes.label: Explicit Bounds Policy
nodes.plain_language: Every repeated or cyclic composition declares a maximum round, budget, deadline, or exhaustion route.
nodes.claim: Cycles and retries are never implicit.

source_refs.selector: Every cycle declares a bound and exhaustion route

nodes.owner_route: Work-definition owner plus applicable budget owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a universal termination proof or permission to retry effects.

nodes.label: Domain Meaning Separation Policy
nodes.plain_language: Structural routing observes declared events but never decides business truth, approval, result quality, or artifact meaning.
nodes.claim: Domain judgment remains in work-owned gates and adapters.

source_refs.selector: Anything that requires domain judgment belongs in a work unit

nodes.owner_route: Each applicable domain meaning and decision owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A route label, terminal event, or projection is not a semantic verdict.

nodes.label: External Effect Boundary Policy
nodes.plain_language: Every external effect crosses an exact adapter with an accepted authority reference and idempotency boundary.
nodes.claim: Structural readiness alone cannot release an external effect.

source_refs.selector: Every external effect crosses an adapter with an accepted authority reference

nodes.owner_route: Applicable exact-effect owner plus selected adapter owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a permission grant, credential, provider selection, or proof of exactly-once business effect.
open_questions: What minimal authority reference may a future kernel verify without owning policy?

nodes.label: Work Definition
nodes.plain_language: An immutable versioned description of one typed leaf or composite work boundary.
nodes.claim: Definition identity remains distinct from run and attempt identity.

source_refs.selector: A definition is immutable and versioned

nodes.owner_route: Work-definition owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a run, attempt, mutable state, or capability grant.

nodes.label: Work Graph
nodes.plain_language: Typed work nodes connected by explicit event-triggered edges and input mappings.
nodes.claim: A future graph must be compiled from exact DomainSpec source rather than independently authored here.
nodes.owner_route: Future DomainSpec work-orchestration source and compiler owners
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not canonical source, communication permission, runtime state, or implementation evidence.

nodes.label: Work Run
nodes.plain_language: One root invocation of one exact work definition.
nodes.claim: Nested paths remain addressed operations inside one root run.
nodes.owner_route: Future accepted work-orchestration runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a definition, attempt, nested scheduler, or global status owner.

nodes.label: Accepted Work History
nodes.plain_language: Ordered accepted structural events retained for replay and audit.
nodes.claim: The owner and exact authority of accepted history remain unresolved.
nodes.owner_route: Unresolved accepted-history owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not automatically the authoritative record of a leaf's domain state.
open_questions: Is accepted history authoritative emitted state or durable evidence copied from a work-owned store?

nodes.label: Orchestration Cursor
nodes.plain_language: A rebuildable structural projection used to avoid duplicate delivery and evaluate releases.
nodes.claim: The cursor is derived, versioned, and non-authoritative for domain meaning.
nodes.owner_route: Future accepted work-orchestration runtime owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not confirmation, current domain truth, effect success, or a mutable canonical work definition.

nodes.label: Executor Adapter
nodes.plain_language: The typed boundary between structural commands and one work-specific execution mechanism.
nodes.claim: Adapters preserve work ownership and return declared events or artifact references.
nodes.owner_route: Future selected realization owner plus bound work owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not an implicit tool grant, credential, provider API, communication permission, or effect authorization.

nodes.label: Domain Gate
nodes.plain_language: A work-owned decision that emits one declared route label and retains its own evidence and meaning.
nodes.claim: The orchestrator routes a gate result but never makes the decision.

source_refs.selector: The gate owns the decision and its evidence

nodes.owner_route: Applicable domain decision owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not a structural quorum, route label, orchestrator decision, or transferable effect permission.

nodes.label: Recursive Work Orchestrator Kernel
nodes.plain_language: A proposal-only thin runtime that may later realize part of this Product Capability.
nodes.claim: The current source is supporting architecture evidence only; no binding is selected.

source_refs.selector: This document proposes a domain-independent orchestration kernel

nodes.owner_route: Future selected RWO realization owner
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Not the Product Capability, an implementation, an accepted specification, runtime conformance, or authority grant.
open_questions: Which owner may accept an exact RWO realization after DomainSpec and system-ontology gates?
